Better Dressings

KITCHEN NOTES / BUILD FLAVOR

Make a simple lemon dressing

Whisk, taste, adjust. A good dressing should bring the salad together without hiding the ingredients.

Whisk → Taste → Adjust
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Start with the recipe amounts

    Put the measured lemon juice and olive oil into a small bowl. Add the seasonings listed in your recipe.

    Look for Use the recipe as your starting point: lemons vary in sharpness.

  2. 02

    Whisk until combined

    Whisk briskly with a fork or small whisk, bringing the oil and lemon juice together.

    Look for The mixture looks slightly cloudy. It may separate again as it stands.

  3. 03

    Taste it on an ingredient

    Dip a piece of cucumber or a chickpea into the dressing. Taste the combination, not just the dressing on its own.

    Look for You should still taste the vegetable or bean underneath the lemon.

  4. 04

    Make one small adjustment

    Too sharp? Whisk in a little more oil. Too oily or flat? Try a little more lemon. Taste again before changing anything else.

    Look for Whisk once more just before using, then add gradually to the salad.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

On a bite of salad, the dressing tastes bright and rounded rather than overwhelmingly sour or oily.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Adding several extra ingredients at once to fix the flavor.

Small adjustments make it easier to understand what the dressing needs.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Change one thing in a small amount, then taste again.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

No lemon? A mild vinegar can provide acidity. Add it gradually and taste: different vinegars have different strengths, so do not assume an identical swap.

Why has the dressing separated?

Oil and lemon juice do not stay mixed on their own. Separation is expected in this simple dressing. Whisk again before pouring; it does not mean the recipe has failed.
